_law: WS06 (audit 2026-11-05 item 6): research answers may only RELEASE after a server-enforced action/citation check — in TypeScript (lib/chat/answer-release.ts, wired by lib/chat/web-tool-loop.ts) and in Rust (crates/ruke-server/src/chat/answer_release.rs, wired by chat/web_loop.rs). This matrix is the ONE truth for the release/diagnosis semantics: both sides read these exact bytes (vitest reads this file; Rust include_str!'s it). No brand/site rules — inputs are generic. The 2026-11-13 brief CLOSED the MHR-D feedback lifecycle: answer content streams LIVE byte-identical, terminal frames park until release, and the release audit enforces CITATION INTEGRITY ONLY (an [S#] marker that resolves to NO server-minted source is a broken reference — its bytes are stripped with residue cleanup; research-claiming wording on a turn with empty citations and no retrieved action gets the ledger-computed SERVER_CHECK_LINE prepended). The harness NEVER erases released text, NEVER injects a model-facing feedback message, and NEVER regenerates an answer because a heuristic flagged it; the diagnosis (diagnose.cases) is INTERNAL SERVER TELEMETRY ONLY — it rides the server log (logger.warn / tracing::warn!), never the user's history, titles, exports, or the model's payload. serverCheckLine stays a server attestation computed from the turn's action ledger (a fact about the harness, not a content rewrite). Detector laws the matrix pins: (P) volatile-fact detectors are lexical PRIORS — they over-match (a '%' in CSS, a price word in a question) and under-match; they decide NOTHING user-visible, only the log. (D) DATE VALIDITY: an a/b/c numeral triple is a date ONLY if it reads plausibly as m/d/y or d/m/y with a 2-4 digit year — 31/39/40 (compiler line numbers) is NOT a date, 05/12/2026 and 12/05/2026 are. (I) CITATION IDENTITY: a resolvable [S#] proves the reference resolves, not that its passage supports the sentence — a flagged sentence is REPORTED regardless of a resolvable marker, an adjacent valid marker, or hedge words. (H) HEDGE LAW: the word 'unverified' does not bypass the report. (S) SEGMENTATION: fenced blocks and inline code are byte-protected on release and invisible to diagnosis. Sections: `cases` pin the release audit; `diagnose.cases` pin the telemetry report shape (date law + hedge law included); `separation` pins that a diagnosed sentence still releases integrity-only — diagnosis never changes a byte the human sees.

diagnose._law: 2026-11-13 brief: the diagnosis is INTERNAL SERVER TELEMETRY — the same detectors as the audit, reporting only, written to the SERVER LOG (logger.warn / tracing::warn!). It rewrites nothing, erases nothing, and never reaches the human UI or the model's payload: the harness does not lecture the model, retract a streamed answer, or regenerate on a heuristic flag. A flagged sentence may be a FALSE POSITIVE (a re-stated user constraint, CSS percentages, compiler line numbers) — that is acceptable precisely because a flag decides nothing user-visible. Laws: DATE VALIDITY (a/b/c is a date only when plausible as m/d/y or d/m/y with a 2-4 digit year — line-number/ratio triples are not dates); CITATION IDENTITY (a resolvable [S#] means the reference resolves, NOT that the sentence is semantically supported — an unsupported volatile sentence with a resolvable marker is still reported when its own marker fails to resolve; a sentence with only resolvable markers is skipped, the documented identity-vs-support limitation); HEDGE LAW (the word 'unverified' never bypasses the report); SEGMENTATION (fenced/inline code invisible, same byte-protection law as the audit).

separation._law: MHR-F (WS26, 2026-11-06) + the 2026-11-13 brief: CITATION INTEGRITY and SEMANTIC SUPPORT are separate concerns with separate owners. Integrity is the HARNESS's: the [S#] grammar is minted by the server, so a marker resolving to NO minted source is a broken reference — the release path strips the marker bytes (whitespace/punctuation residue cleanup only) and NEVER otherwise touches the sentence's words. A marker that DOES resolve is never removed, moved or altered, even when an adjacent marker in the same sentence is fabricated. Semantic SUPPORT is the MODEL's — and since 2026-11-13 the harness's diagnosis is INTERNAL TELEMETRY ONLY: it never reaches the model as a message, never retracts streamed text, and never triggers a regeneration. releaseCases pin the release law; separationCases pin that the SAME input still DIAGNOSES (log-only) while releasing integrity-only — a diagnosis flag changes ZERO bytes the human sees, false-positive volatile matches included. Known limitation (documented, not hidden): the diagnosis cannot see the human's own turn, so a re-stated user constraint is still reported as telemetry — harmless, since telemetry decides nothing. releaseCases are shared byte-for-byte with `cases`.
